Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 4, verse 1:

(p-446) Surat al-Nisa' (The Women)

Madaniyya (revealed in Madina), except for one verse, which was revealed in Makka concerning Uthman ibn Talha, when the Prophet (ﷺ) wanted to take the keys of the Ka'ba and hand them over to his uncle al-Abbas. It is the verse of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render the trusts to their rightful owners﴾.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from a single soul﴾ means Adam. In this there is a blessing upon you, because it is closer to fostering compassion among you.

﴿And created from it its mate﴾ means Eve. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Hasan said: she was created from a rib of Adam. It was said: from the left one. For this reason it was said of the woman: a crooked rib.

﴿And from the two of them He spread forth many men and women﴾. It was narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said when this verse was revealed to him: ("The woman was created from the man, so her concern is with the man, and the man was created from dust, so his concern is with the dust.") (p-447)

﴿And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs﴾. The meaning of His saying "through whom you ask one another" is their saying: "I ask you by Allah and by the womb (kinship)." This is the saying of Mujahid and Ibrahim. Hamza recited "wa-al-arhami" with a kasra (al-arhāmi) according to this meaning.

Regarding "al-arham" (wombs/kinship ties) there is another opinion: that it means "maintain them and do not sever them." This is the saying of Qatada and al-Suddi, because Allah, Exalted is He, intended at the beginning of the surah, when He informed them that they were from a single soul, that they should maintain ties with one another and know that they are brothers even if they are distant.

﴿Indeed, Allah has ever been over you an Watcher﴾. In this there are two interpretations: the first is "Protector," which is the saying of Mujahid.

The second is "All-Knowing," which is the saying of Ibn Zayd.

[p. 448]

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And give to the orphans their property, and do not substitute the bad [of your own] for the good [of theirs]﴾. There are four interpretations of this:

The first is: the unlawful in exchange for the lawful. This is the view of Mujahid.

The second is: that one makes the counterfeit (*za'if*) in place of the good, and the lean in place of the fat, and says, "A dirham for a dirham, a sheep for a sheep." This is the view of Ibn al-Musayyab, al-Zuhri, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi.

The third is: hastening to consume the unlawful before the lawful comes. This is the meaning of Mujahid's view as well.

The fourth is: that the people of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance) did not give inheritance to the young children and the women, and the eldest man would take it [all]. So he would substitute the bad for the good, because his share of the inheritance was good, while his taking the whole was bad. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

﴿And do not consume their property with your property﴾: that is, together with your property. It means that they mix it with their own property so that it becomes part of their own responsibility, and then they consume its profit.

﴿Indeed, that is ever a great sin (*huban kabiran*)﴾. The *hub* is sin. From it comes the saying of the people, "So-and-so *tahawwaba* from such-and-such," meaning he avoided it. The poet said:

*For two emigrants surrounded him, on a day when they had certainly erred and sinned.*

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "When this verse was revealed concerning the property of orphans, they disliked mixing with them, and the guardian of an orphan would separate his property from the orphan's property. So they complained of that to the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿They ask you about orphans. Say, 'Improving their condition is best; and if you mix your affairs with theirs, then they are your brothers﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:220]." That is, mix with them, but fear their sin.

﴿And if you fear that you will not be just with orphans, then marry what seems good to you of women﴾. There are four interpretations of this:

The first: it means, if you fear that you will not be just in marrying orphan girls, then marry what is lawful to you of other women. This is the view of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

The second: they used to fear not being just with the property of orphans, but they did not fear not being just with women. So Allah revealed this verse, meaning: just as you feared not being just with the property of orphans, so also fear not being just with women. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, and Qatadah.

The third: they used to guard against the property of orphans but did not guard against adultery (*zina*). So He said: just as you feared [wrongdoing] regarding the property of orphans, then fear adultery, and marry what seems good to you of women. This is the view of Mujahid.

The fourth: the reason for its revelation was that in the Jahiliyyah, the Quraysh used to marry many women without any restricted number. When one of them had many wives and their maintenance burdened him and his wealth was little, he would reach out to the property of orphans that he had. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And if you fear that you will not be just with orphans, then marry what seems good to you of women﴾.

Regarding His saying ﴿what seems good to you of women﴾, there are two views:

One: that this refers to women, and its meaning is: marry from among the women what is lawful.

This is the view of al-Farra'.

The second: that this refers to the marriage, and its meaning is: marry women in a good (*tayyib*) marriage.

This is the view of Mujahid.

﴿Two, three, or four﴾: an estimate of their number and a limit on those whose marriage is permitted among them. This is the view of 'Ikrimah.

﴿Mathna, thulath, andruba'﴾ are formed with a change from *ithnayn* (two), *thalath* (three), and *arba'* (four). Likewise, *uhad* and *mawhad* (one), *thunaa* and *mathna* (two), *thulath* and *mathlath* (three), and *ruba'* and *marba'* (four). These are forms of numbers that are definite in meaning, and poetry has come with the like of this. Tamim ibn Abi Muqbil said:

*You see the blue (rubbed) marks under his chest, singly and in pairs, his shoulder-bones having weakened them.*

Another said:

*We killed by him, from among you, some in twos and ones, [and] with four of you, and another, the fifth.*

Abu 'Ubaydah said: "Nothing has been heard from the Arabs of changing what exceeds *ruba'* and *marba'* from its own form except in a verse of al-Kumayt, for he said regarding ten, *'ushar*, in his saying:

*So they did not rest from you until you were fatigued, [you who are] above men in qualities, [as] tens (ushar).*"

Abu Hatim said: "Rather, it has come in their speech from one up to ten." And he recited the poet's saying:

*I struck with a Abshami blow that turned the six (sudas) so that they would not stand straight.*

﴿And if you fear that you will not be just﴾: meaning among the four wives, ﴿then [only] one﴾: meaning one of the women.

﴿Or those your right hands possess﴾: meaning among the slave-women.

﴿That is more suitable that you not incline toward injustice (*an la ta'ulu*)﴾. There are three views concerning it:

The first: that you not have many dependents whom you support. This is the view of al-Shafi'i.

The second: its meaning is that you not go astray. This is the view of Ibn Ishaq, which he narrated from Mujahid.

The third: that you not deviate from the truth and act unjustly. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, and 'Ikrimah.

The root of *al-'awl* is going beyond the limit, and from it comes *'awl al-fara'id* (the "exceeding" of the inheritance shares), because they go beyond the limit of the specified portions. 'Ikrimah recited a verse of Abu Talib:

*With a scale of justice that does not cheat by a grain, and a weigher of truthfulness whose weighing is not inclined (ghayr 'a'il).*

That is, not deviating.

'Uthman ibn 'Affan wrote to the people of Kufa about something they had reproached him for: "I am not a scale of justice that inclines (la a'ul)." [p. 451]

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And give the women their dowries (*sudaqatihinna*)﴾. There is a disagreement about to whom this address is directed, with two views:

One: that it is directed to the husbands. This is the view of the majority.

The second: that it is directed to the guardians (*awliya'*), because in the Jahiliyyah they used to take possession of a woman's dowry. So Allah commanded that their dowries be delivered to them. This is the view of Abu Salih.

As for *nihlah*, it is a gift without any return. The religion was called *nihlah* because it is a gift from Allah. Regarding the naming of the bee (*nahl*) with this, there are two views: One: it was called *nahl* because of the honey it gives. The second: because Allah the Exalted gave it (*nahalahu*) to His servants.

Regarding the meaning of *nihlah* in the dowry, there are four interpretations: The first: it means a specified obligation (*fari<u>d</u>ah musamma*). This is the view of Qatadah and Ibn Jurayj.

The second: that it is a gift from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to them after it had been the possession of the guardians. This is the view of Abu Salih.

The third: that it is a prohibition against what they used to do, of the *shighar* proposal (*khutbat al-shighar*) and marriage without a dowry. This is the view of Sulayman ibn Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mu'tamir.

The fourth: that it means they should be content (*yatibu nafsan*) in giving it, just as they are content in giving a gift and a present. This is the view of some of the later scholars.

﴿And if they give you willingly (*tibna lakum*) of it, [any] part of it, then consume it with satisfaction and ease (*hanian mari'an*)﴾: meaning the wives, if they willingly give up some of their dowry to their husbands, according to the view of those who made it an address to the husbands, and to their guardians according to the view of those who made it an address to the guardians.

﴿Consume it with satisfaction and ease﴾. *Al-hani'* is what results in benefit and healing. From it comes *hana'a al-ba'ir*, meaning the camel was healed. The poet said:

*Changing, his noble qualities appear; he places the healing salve (hana') in the places of the sores (nuqab).*

Those who held the continuing of its ruling on the first basis differed regarding an heir who is a minor: must his guardian take it out from his share? On two views: one of them, that it is obligatory, is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id, and the guardian says to them a kind word.

The second: it is an obligatory right upon the guardians in the property of minors, and this is the view of 'Ubaydah and al-Hasan.

﴿And speak to them a kind word﴾. Concerning it there are two views. The first: it is an address to the heirs and their guardians, that they should speak to those present from the close relatives, orphans and the needy a kind word when giving them the wealth. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The second: it is an address to others, that they should speak to the heirs who give a kind word, namely supplication for them for provision and sufficiency.

(p-457)

﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them. So let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice﴾. Concerning it there are four opinions. The first: its meaning is: let those who attend a dying person who makes a bequest of his wealth beware of urging him to distribute his wealth as bequests to those who do not inherit from him, but rather let them urge him to keep his wealth for his children, just as if they were the ones making the bequest they would prefer that their wealth remain for their children. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and al-Suddi.

The second: its meaning is: let those who attend the deceased while he bequeaths beware of forbidding him from bequeathing to his relatives, and of ordering him to hold back his wealth and preserve it for his children; for if they were relatives of the testator they would prefer that he bequeath to them. This is the view of Miqsam and Sulayman ibn al-Mu'tamir.

The third: that this is a command from Allah, may He be exalted, to the guardians of orphans, that they should look after them with goodness regarding their persons and their wealth, just as they would wish the guardians of their young children after them to treat them with goodness, had they died and left their children as young orphans. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas.

The fourth: that whoever fears for his offspring after him, and loves that Allah should avert harm from them after his death, then let him fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice. This is the view of Abu Bishr ibn al-Daylami.

﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾. He expressed the taking by "consuming," because it is the purpose of taking.

﴿They consume not but fire into their bellies﴾. Concerning it there are two views. The first: it means that they will lead to the Fire by it.

The second: their bellies will be filled with it as a punishment that necessitates the Fire.

﴿And they will burn in a Blaze﴾. Al-Si'lu is the necessity of the Fire, and al-Sa'ir is the kindling of the Fire, and from it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the Hellfire is set ablaze﴾ [al-Takwir: 12].

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 4, verse 11:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾. Al-Suddi narrated, saying: "The people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) would not give inheritance to girls or to weak boys. They would not give a man's inheritance from his offspring except to one who was able to fight. So ʿAbd al-Rahman, the brother of Hassan the poet, died and left a wife called Umm Kujjah, and he left five sisters. The heirs came and took his property. Umm Kujjah complained of that to the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah, Exalted is He, revealed this verse."

﴿And if there are women more than two, then for them is two-thirds of what he left﴾. So He prescribed for three or more daughters, when they are alone without a male, two-thirds, and He prescribed for one daughter, when she is alone, a half. The scholars differed concerning two daughters. Ibn ʿAbbas said: a half, on account of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿more than two﴾. The majority held that their prescribed share is two-thirds, like three or more, by analogy with sisters.

Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And for his parents, to each one of them, a sixth﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: the property used to belong to the children, and the bequest was to the parents and the nearest relatives. Allah, Exalted is He, abrogated that (naskh, the lifting of an earlier ruling by a later one), so He made for the male what is equal to the share of two females, and made for the parents, to each one of them, a sixth.

Then He said: ﴿after any bequest he may have made or debt﴾... ﴿whichever of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾. Then He said: ﴿From what he leaves, if he has children. But if he has no children and the parents inherit from him, then for his mother is one-third﴾. He equalized between each of the two parents, in the presence of a child, in that each of them has a sixth. Then He made a distinction between them in the absence of a child, in that He made for the mother one-third and the remainder for the father. This was so because the two parents, in the presence of a child, inherit a fixed share by reason of the parenthood in which they are equal, so He equalized between their fixed shares. When there is no child, the mother inherits a fixed share because there is no agnatic (ʿasabah, residuary) element in her case, and the father inherits by way of residuary (taʿsib), because it is the stronger inheritance; and He made her fixed share half of what the father takes by his residuary status, so that the male receives what is equal to the share of two females.

﴿But if he has brothers, then for his mother is a sixth﴾. There is no disagreement that three brothers exclude her from the one-third, which is the highest of her shares, down to the sixth, which is the least of it, and the remainder after her sixth goes to the father.

It is reported from Tawus that she returns to the brothers without the father, so that what they have excluded her from returns to them and not to others. This is an error for two reasons: first, that the father excludes whoever is connected through him, like the grandfather; and second, that the residuary heirs have no prescribed share in inheritance, as the sons do.

As for the exclusion of the mother by two brothers, Ibn ʿAbbas prevented it, holding to the apparent plural in His saying: ﴿if he has brothers﴾. The rest of the Companions disagreed with him, excluding the mother by two brothers or more, though she is not excluded by a single brother, because the word in the plural form does not prevent its being placed in the position of the dual, as in His saying: ﴿your hearts have inclined﴾ [al-Tahrim: 4], although the two are, in the matter of the fixed shares, equivalent to the full plural, as with sisters and full or paternal siblings of the mother.

﴿After any bequest he may have made or debt﴾. He placed the debt and the bequest before the inheritance, because the debt is a right upon the deceased, and the bequest is a right of his, and both take precedence over the right of his heirs. Then He placed the debt before the bequest, though in recitation it is later, because what is owed by the deceased as a right is more appropriately given precedence over what is his as a right.

Ibn Ishaq narrated from al-Harith al-Aʿwar, from ʿAli, peace be upon him, who said: "You recite this verse: ﴿after any bequest he may have made or debt﴾, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ decided the debt before the bequest." If it is asked: why did He mention the bequest before the debt, if in ruling it is later? It is said: because "or" (aw) does not necessitate ordering; it only establishes one of two things, singly or combined, so it is as if He said: after one of them or after both of them.

﴿Your fathers and your sons—you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾, meaning in religion or in worldly life.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 4, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if a man or a woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants as heirs, but has a brother or a sister, then each one of them shall receive a sixth﴾. The scholars differed concerning the meaning of kalala (those who inherit without ascendants or descendants) in three opinions. The first: they are all those other than the child (walad), and this is narrated from Ibn Abbas, transmitted by Tawus from him.

The second: they are all those other than the parent (walid), and this is the view of al-Hakam ibn Utayba.

The third: they are all those other than the child and the parent, and this is the view of Abu Bakr and Umar, and the well-known position of Ibn Abbas. (p. 461)

Al-Sha'bi narrated, saying: Abu Bakr said: "I have formed an opinion concerning the kalala. If it is correct, then it is from Allah alone, having no partner; and if it is wrong, then it is from me, and Allah is free of it. The kalala is what lies beyond the parent and the child."

When Umar was appointed caliph, he said: "I am truly ashamed before Allah to oppose Abu Bakr in an opinion he held."

Then the scholars differed concerning what is called kalala, in three opinions. The first: the kalala is the deceased, and this is the view of Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi.

The second: it is the living heir, and this is the view of Ibn Umar.

The third: it is both the deceased and the living heir, and this is the view of Ibn Zayd.

The root meaning of kalala is encompassing, and from it comes al-iklil (the crown), so named because it encircles the head. Likewise, the kalala is so named because it encircles the root of lineage, which is the parent and the child.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 4, verses 13–14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾. Regarding it there are five opinions:

First: they are the conditions of Allah (shurut Allah), and this is the saying of al-Suddi.

Second: they are the obedience to Allah (ta'at Allah), and this is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas.

Third: they are the sunnah of Allah and His command (sunnat Allah wa amruhu).

Fourth: they are the obligations of Allah (fara'id Allah) which He set as limits for His servants.

Fifth: they are the detailed explanations of Allah concerning His obligations (tafsilat Allah li-fara'idihi).

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 4, verse 15–16:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness﴾ — by "lewdness" is meant fornication (zina).

﴿Then call against them four witnesses from among you﴾ — meaning, a clear proof by which the prescribed punishment (hadd) becomes obligatory for them.

﴿And if they testify, then confine them to houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way﴾ — the scholars differed concerning their confinement in houses: is it a hadd (a prescribed punishment), or a promise of the hadd? There are two opinions. ﴿Or Allah ordains for them a way﴾ — by "the way" is meant the hadd. And it is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Take from me, Allah has ordained for them a way: the virgin with the virgin, a hundred lashes and exile for a year; and the previously married (thayyib) with the previously married, a hundred lashes and stoning." The scholars differed on whether the lashing has been abrogated (naskh) from the punishment of the previously married, on two views. The first: it has been abrogated, and this is the view of the majority of the Successors (tabi'un) and the jurists. The second: its ruling remains valid, and this was the view of Qatadah and Dawud ibn Ali. This verse is general concerning the virgin and the previously married, and the scholars differed on its abrogation according to their differing over whether it is a hadd or a promise of the hadd. Whoever said it is a hadd considered it abrogated by the verse of al-Nur (24), and whoever said it is a promise of the hadd considered it to be in force.

His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And the two of you who commit it, harm them﴾ — there are two opinions concerning it. The first: it was revealed specifically concerning virgins, and this is the view of al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd. The second: it is general concerning virgins and previously married persons, and this is the view of al-Hasan and Ata'.

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the two of you who commit it﴾, on two views. The first: it refers to the man and the woman, and this is the view of al-Hasan and Ata'. The second: it refers to the two virgins, male and female, and this is the view of al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd.

Concerning the harm that is commanded, there are three sayings. The first: reproach and rebuke by the tongue, and this is the view of Qatadah, al-Suddi and Mujahid. The second: that it is reproach by the tongue and striking with sandals. The third: that it is unspecified, its explanation being taken for the virgin from the verse of al-Nur, and for the previously married from the Sunnah.

If it is asked: how did the mention of harm come after confinement? There are two answers. The first: this verse was revealed before the first, then He commanded that it be placed after it in recitation; so the harm came first, then confinement, then flogging or stoning. This is the view of al-Hasan. The second: the harm applies specifically to the two virgins, and the confinement to the two previously married; this is the view of al-Suddi.

Then the scholars differed concerning its abrogation according to their differing over its generality and its explanation.

﴿And if they repent and amend, then leave them alone﴾ — meaning, they repent from lewdness and set right their religion; "leave them alone" means pardon them and refrain from harming them.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 4, verses 17–18:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Repentance with Allah is only for those who do evil in ignorance﴾. Scholars have differed about what is meant by "ignorance" (jahala), giving three opinions:

The first: every sin a person commits is done in ignorance, and every disobedient person who disobeys is ignorant. This is the view of Abu al-'Aliyah.

The second: it means they do that deed deliberately, and "ignorance" means deliberateness. This is the view of al-Dahhak and Mujahid.

The third: "ignorance" is doing evil in this world. This is the view of 'Ikrimah.

﴿Then they repent soon﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations. The first: then they repent during their health, before their death and before their illness. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi.

The second: before witnessing the Angel of Death. This is the view of al-Dahhak and Abu Mijlaz.

The third: before death. 'Ikrimah said: "The whole of this world is 'soon'."

Qatadah narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant so long as he has not begun the death rattle (yughargharu)." ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now"﴾, up to His saying: ﴿and they are disbelievers﴾. Concerning this there are two views. The first, which is the view of the majority, is that it was revealed concerning the disobedient among the Muslims. The second is that it was revealed concerning the hypocrites; this is the view of al-Rabi'.

He equated between the one who did not repent until he died and the one who repented at the presence of death, a state which those present at it recognize.

It is possible that it refers to the moment of witnessing (the Angel of Death) in a condition by which it is known, even though one is prevented from reporting it.

**Al-Mawardi, *al-Nukat wa al-'Uyun* (Commentary on Surah 4, verses 19–22)**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force﴾. The occasion of this (revelation) is that the people of Madina, in the pre-Islamic period (al-Jahiliyya), when one of them died leaving a wife, his son or relative had more right to her than others, and more right over her person than she had herself. If he wished, he would marry her himself like his father, with the first dowry. If he wished, he would give her in marriage to someone else and take her dowry. If he wished, he would prevent her from remarrying until she died, so that he inherited her, or until she ransomed herself from him with her dowry. This continued until Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat died, leaving his wife Kubaysha bint Ma'n ibn 'Asim. His son wanted to marry her, so she came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said (p-466):

"O Prophet of Allah, I was not inherited along with my husband, nor was I left free so that I could be married (to whom I choose)." So this verse was revealed.

﴿And do not prevent them (from remarrying) in order to take away part of what you have given them﴾. Concerning this there are four opinions:

The first: it is addressed to the heirs of the husbands, that they [not] prevent the women from remarrying, as we have mentioned. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and 'Ikrima.

The second: it is addressed to the husbands, that they [not] prevent their wives after divorce, as Quraysh used to do in the pre-Islamic period. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

The third: it is addressed to the husbands, that they [not] detain women by force so that they will ransom themselves, or die so that the husband inherits them. This is the view of Qatada, al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak.

The fourth: it is addressed to the guardians (awliya'). This is the view of Mujahid.

﴿Except when they commit a clear immorality﴾. Regarding this there are three opinions:

The first: it is adultery (zina). This is the view of al-Hasan, Abu Qilaba and al-Suddi.

The second: it is disobedience (nushuz). This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and 'A'isha.

The third: it is abusive speech and harm.

It has been narrated from Miqsam, in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "And do not prevent them in order to take away part of what you have given them, except that they commit immorality (yufhishna)." ﴿But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes in it much good﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: this means a righteous child.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you desire to replace a wife with another wife, and you have given one of them a heap of gold, do not take anything from it﴾. This means that they (the wives) have come to own the dowry, and their ownership of it is not conditional upon remaining with them; rather, it is theirs whether they stay (married) or separate.

﴿Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?﴾ Concerning this there are two statements: the first is that it means taking it unjustly through slander. The second is that (the husband) would slander her, so that he might take it back from her.

The reason this is forbidden in the case of replacing them is that it is forbidden even if he does not replace them. This is so that no one would imagine that it is permissible, when he replaces her with another, to take what he gave her in order to give it to the one he has replaced her with, even though that is covered by the general prohibition.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And how could you take it when you have gone in unto one another?﴾ Concerning this there are two statements: the first is that "al-ifda'" means intercourse (al-jima'). This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and al-Suddi. The second is that it means seclusion (al-khalwa). This is the view of Abu Hanifa.

﴿And they have taken from you a solemn covenant﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions: the first is that it is the marriage contract by which intimacy is made lawful. This is the view of Mujahid. The second is that it is "retaining (the wife) with kindness or releasing her with goodness." This is the view of al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin and Qatada. The third is what Musa ibn 'Ubayda narrated from Su'da ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, women are with you as captives (ʿawan). You have taken them under the trust of Allah, and you have made their private parts lawful by the word of Allah. Your right over them is that they do not allow anyone to sit on your bedding, and that they do not disobey you in what is reasonable. If they do so, then their provision and clothing are due to them in a reasonable manner."

There is a difference of opinion regarding whether this ruling is established or abrogated (naskh, the replacement of a ruling by a later one), on two views. The first: it is muhkam (established and not abrogated), and it is not permissible for him to take anything of what he gave her, whether she was the one who wanted the divorce or he was (p-468). This is the view of Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani.

The second: it is abrogated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

Abu Ja'far al-Tabari and others said: its ruling remains valid, except when there is fear of disobedience (nushuz), in which case it is permissible for him to take a ransom from her.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred﴾. Concerning this there are four opinions:

The first: it was revealed concerning people who used to inherit their fathers' wives. Islam came with the prohibition of this, and pardoned what had occurred of it among them in the pre-Islamic period, so that they would not be held accountable for it if they avoided it in Islam. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada, 'Ata' and 'Ikrima.

The second: meaning, do not marry as your fathers married in the pre-Islamic period in a corrupt manner, except what has already passed among you in your pre-Islamic time, for that is pardoned if it is of a kind that may be permitted to continue. This is the view of some of the Successors (tabi'un).

The third: its meaning is: do not marry those women whom your fathers married in a valid marriage, except what has already passed among them in fornication and illicit intercourse, for marrying them is lawful for you, since they were not lawful (to them); rather, their marriage was (a matter of) immorality, abhorrence and an evil way. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

The fourth: "except what has already passed, so leave it, for you will be held accountable for it." They said this, and this is an exception of the disconnected kind (istithna' munqati'), and some of them took it to mean "but" (lakin).

﴿Indeed, it was an immorality and abhorrence﴾. Al-maqt is intense hatred because of the ugliness of the one who commits it. From it comes their saying: "The people abhorred him" (qad maqatahu al-nas) when they hated him, and "a man who is maqit (abhorred)." It used to be said that a man's child from his father's wife is "al-maqti."

﴿And it was an evil way﴾, meaning a path.

**Al-Mawardi, *al-Nukat wa al-'Uyun* (Commentary on Surah 4, verses 19–22)**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force﴾. The occasion of this (revelation) is that the people of Madina, in the pre-Islamic period (al-Jahiliyya), when one of them died leaving a wife, his son or relative had more right to her than others, and more right over her person than she had herself. If he wished, he would marry her himself like his father, with the first dowry. If he wished, he would give her in marriage to someone else and take her dowry. If he wished, he would prevent her from remarrying until she died, so that he inherited her, or until she ransomed herself from him with her dowry. This continued until Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat died, leaving his wife Kubaysha bint Ma'n ibn 'Asim. His son wanted to marry her, so she came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said (p-466):

"O Prophet of Allah, I was not inherited along with my husband, nor was I left free so that I could be married (to whom I choose)." So this verse was revealed.

﴿And do not prevent them (from remarrying) in order to take away part of what you have given them﴾. Concerning this there are four opinions:

The first: it is addressed to the heirs of the husbands, that they [not] prevent the women from remarrying, as we have mentioned. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and 'Ikrima.

The second: it is addressed to the husbands, that they [not] prevent their wives after divorce, as Quraysh used to do in the pre-Islamic period. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

The third: it is addressed to the husbands, that they [not] detain women by force so that they will ransom themselves, or die so that the husband inherits them. This is the view of Qatada, al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak.

The fourth: it is addressed to the guardians (awliya'). This is the view of Mujahid.

﴿Except when they commit a clear immorality﴾. Regarding this there are three opinions:

The first: it is adultery (zina). This is the view of al-Hasan, Abu Qilaba and al-Suddi.

The second: it is disobedience (nushuz). This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and 'A'isha.

The third: it is abusive speech and harm.

It has been narrated from Miqsam, in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "And do not prevent them in order to take away part of what you have given them, except that they commit immorality (yufhishna)." ﴿But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes in it much good﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: this means a righteous child.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you desire to replace a wife with another wife, and you have given one of them a heap of gold, do not take anything from it﴾. This means that they (the wives) have come to own the dowry, and their ownership of it is not conditional upon remaining with them; rather, it is theirs whether they stay (married) or separate.

﴿Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?﴾ Concerning this there are two statements: the first is that it means taking it unjustly through slander. The second is that (the husband) would slander her, so that he might take it back from her.

The reason this is forbidden in the case of replacing them is that it is forbidden even if he does not replace them. This is so that no one would imagine that it is permissible, when he replaces her with another, to take what he gave her in order to give it to the one he has replaced her with, even though that is covered by the general prohibition.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And how could you take it when you have gone in unto one another?﴾ Concerning this there are two statements: the first is that "al-ifda'" means intercourse (al-jima'). This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and al-Suddi. The second is that it means seclusion (al-khalwa). This is the view of Abu Hanifa.

﴿And they have taken from you a solemn covenant﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions: the first is that it is the marriage contract by which intimacy is made lawful. This is the view of Mujahid. The second is that it is "retaining (the wife) with kindness or releasing her with goodness." This is the view of al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin and Qatada. The third is what Musa ibn 'Ubayda narrated from Su'da ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, women are with you as captives (ʿawan). You have taken them under the trust of Allah, and you have made their private parts lawful by the word of Allah. Your right over them is that they do not allow anyone to sit on your bedding, and that they do not disobey you in what is reasonable. If they do so, then their provision and clothing are due to them in a reasonable manner."

There is a difference of opinion regarding whether this ruling is established or abrogated (naskh, the replacement of a ruling by a later one), on two views. The first: it is muhkam (established and not abrogated), and it is not permissible for him to take anything of what he gave her, whether she was the one who wanted the divorce or he was (p-468). This is the view of Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani.

The second: it is abrogated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

Abu Ja'far al-Tabari and others said: its ruling remains valid, except when there is fear of disobedience (nushuz), in which case it is permissible for him to take a ransom from her.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred﴾. Concerning this there are four opinions:

The first: it was revealed concerning people who used to inherit their fathers' wives. Islam came with the prohibition of this, and pardoned what had occurred of it among them in the pre-Islamic period, so that they would not be held accountable for it if they avoided it in Islam. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada, 'Ata' and 'Ikrima.

The second: meaning, do not marry as your fathers married in the pre-Islamic period in a corrupt manner, except what has already passed among you in your pre-Islamic time, for that is pardoned if it is of a kind that may be permitted to continue. This is the view of some of the Successors (tabi'un).

The third: its meaning is: do not marry those women whom your fathers married in a valid marriage, except what has already passed among them in fornication and illicit intercourse, for marrying them is lawful for you, since they were not lawful (to them); rather, their marriage was (a matter of) immorality, abhorrence and an evil way. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

The fourth: "except what has already passed, so leave it, for you will be held accountable for it." They said this, and this is an exception of the disconnected kind (istithna' munqati'), and some of them took it to mean "but" (lakin).

﴿Indeed, it was an immorality and abhorrence﴾. Al-maqt is intense hatred because of the ugliness of the one who commits it. From it comes their saying: "The people abhorred him" (qad maqatahu al-nas) when they hated him, and "a man who is maqit (abhorred)." It used to be said that a man's child from his father's wife is "al-maqti."

﴿And it was an evil way﴾, meaning a path.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكم أُمَّهاتُكُمْ﴾ إلى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إلا ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكُمْ﴾ فِيهِ أرْبَعَةُ أقاوِيلَ: أحَدُها: والمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ النِّساءِ يَعْنِي ذَواتَ الأزْواجِ إلّا ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكم بِالسَّبْيِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ عَلِيٍّ، وابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وأبِي قِلابَةَ، والزُّهْرِيِّ، ومَكْحُولٍ، وابْنِ زَيْدٍ.

وَقَدْ رَوى عُثْمانُ البَتِّيُّ عَنْ أبِي خَلِيلٍ عَنْ أبِي سَعِيدٍ الخُدْرِيِّ قالَ: «لَما سَبى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ أهْلَ أوْطاسَ، قُلْنا: يا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، كَيْفَ نَقَعُ عَلى نِساءٍ قَدْ عَرَفْنا أنْسابَهُنَّ وأزْواجَهُنَّ؟ قالَ: فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ» ﴿والمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ النِّساءِ إلا ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكُمْ﴾. والثّانِي: أنَّ المُحْصَناتِ ذَواتُ الأزْواجِ حَرامٌ عَلى غَيْرِ أزْواجِهِنَّ إلّا ما (p-٤٧٠)

مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكم مِنَ الإماءِ، إذا اشْتَراها مُشْتَرٍ بَطَلَ نِكاحُها وحَلَّتْ لِمُشْتَرِيها ويَكُونُ بَيْعُها طَلاقَها، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، وأُبَيِّ بْنِ كَعْبٍ، وجابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، وأنَسِ بْنِ مالِكٍ، وابْنِ عَبّاسٍ في رِوايَةِ عِكْرِمَةَ عَنْهُ، وسَعِيدِ بْنِ المُسَيِّبِ، والحَسَنِ. قالَ الحَسَنُ: طَلاقُ الأمَةِ يُثْبِتُ نَسَبَها، وبَيْعَها، وعِتْقَها، وهِبَتَها، ومِيراثَها، وطَلاقَ زَوْجِها.

الثّالِثُ: أنَّ المُحْصَناتِ مِنَ النِّساءِ العَفائِفُ إلّا ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكم بِعَقْدِ النِّكاحِ، أوْ مِلْكِ اليَمِينِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ عُمَرَ، وسَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، وأبِي العالِيَةِ، وعَبِيدَةَ السَّلْمانِيِّ، وعَطاءٍ، والسُّدِّيِّ.

والرّابِعُ: أنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ نَزَلَتْ في نِساءٍ كُنَّ هاجَرْنَ إلى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ ولَهُنَّ أزْواجٌ، فَتَزَوَّجَهُنَّ المُسْلِمُونَ، ثُمَّ قَدِمَ أزْواجُهُنَّ مُهاجِرِينَ، فَنُهِيَ المُسْلِمُونَ عَنْ نِكاحِهِنَّ، وهَذا قَوْلُ أبِي سَعِيدٍ الخُدْرِيِّ.

وَأصْلُ الإحْصانِ المَنعُ، ومِنهُ حِصْنُ البَلَدِ، لِأنَّهُ يَمْنَعُ مِنَ العَدُوِّ، ودِرْعٌ حَصِينَةٌ أيْ مَنِيعَةٌ، وفَرَسٌ حِصانٌ، لِأنَّ صاحِبَهُ يَمْتَنِعُ بِهِ مِنَ الهَلَكَةِ، وامْرَأةٌ حَصانٌ، وهي العَفِيفَةُ لِأنَّها تَمْتَنِعُ مِنَ الفاحِشَةِ، ومِنهُ ﴿وَمَرْيَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرانَ الَّتِي أحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها﴾ [التَّحْرِيمِ: ١٢]. ﴿كِتابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أوْجُهٍ: أحَدُها: أنَّ مَعْناهُ: حُرِّمَ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْكم كِتابًا مِنَ اللَّهِ.

والثّانِي: مَعْناهُ الزَمُوا كِتابَ اللَّهِ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّ كِتابَ اللَّهِ قَيِّمٌ عَلَيْكم فِيما تَسْتَحِلُّونَهُ وتُحَرِّمُونَهُ.

﴿وَأُحِلَّ لَكم ما وراءَ ذَلِكُمْ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أقاوِيلَ: أحَدُها: أنَّ مَعْناهُ ما دُونَ الخُمُسِ، وهو قَوْلُ السُّدِّيِّ.

والثّانِي: ما وراءَ ذَواتِ المَحارِمِ مِن أقارِبِكم، وهو قَوْلُ عَطاءٍ.

والثّالِثُ: ما وراءَ ذَلِكم مِمّا مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكم، وهو قَوْلُ قَتادَةَ.

﴿أنْ تَبْتَغُوا بِأمْوالِكُمْ﴾ يَعْنِي أنْ تَلْتَمِسُوا بِأمْوالِكم إمّا شِراءً بِثَمَنٍ، أوْ نِكاحًا بِصَداقٍ. (p-٤٧١)

﴿مُحْصِنِينَ غَيْرَ مُسافِحِينَ﴾ يَعْنِي مُتَناكِحِينَ غَيْرَ زانِينَ، وأصْلُ السِّفاحِ صَبُّ الماءِ، ومِنهُ سَفَحَ الدَّمْعَ إذا صَبَّهُ، وسَفْحُ الجَبَلِ أسْفَلُهُ لِأنَّهُ مَصَبُّ الماءِ فِيهِ، وسِفاحُ الزِّنى لِصَبِّ مائِهِ حَرامًا.

﴿فَما اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنهُنَّ فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً﴾ أيْ آتُوهُنَّ صَدُقاتِهِنَّ مَعْلُومَةً، وهَذا قَوْلُ مُجاهِدٍ، والحَسَنِ، وأحَدُ قَوْلَيِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّها المُتْعَةُ إلى أجَلٍ مُسَمًّى مِن غَيْرِ نِكاحٍ، قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: كانَ في قِراءَةِ أُبَيٍّ: فَما اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنهُنَّ إلى أجَلٍ مُسَمّى، وكانَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ كَذَلِكَ يَقْرَأُ، وسَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، وهَذا قَوْلُ السُّدِّيِّ. وقالَ الحَكَمُ: قالَ عَلِيٌّ: لَوْلا أنَّ عُمَرَ نَهى عَنِ المُتْعَةِ ما زَنى إلّا شَقِيٌّ، وهَذا لا يَثْبُتُ، والمَحْكِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ خِلافُهُ، وأنَّهُ تابَ مِنَ المُتْعَةِ ورِبا النَّقْدِ.

﴿وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكم فِيما تَراضَيْتُمْ بِهِ مِن بَعْدِ الفَرِيضَةِ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أقاوِيلَ: أحَدُها: مَعْناهُ لا حَرَجَ عَلَيْكم أيُّها الأزْواجُ إنْ أُعْسِرْتُمْ بَعْدَ أنْ فَرَضْتُمْ لِنِسائِكم مَهْرًا عَنْ تَراضٍ أنْ يَنْقُصْنَكم مِنهُ ويَتْرُكْنَكم، وهَذا قَوْلُ سُلَيْمانَ بْنِ المُعْتَمِرِ.

والثّانِي: لا جُناحَ عَلَيْكم أيُّها النّاسُ فِيما تَراضَيْتُمْ أنْتُمْ والنِّساءُ اللَّواتِي اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِنَّ إلى أجَلٍ مُسَمًّى، إذا انْقَضى الأجَلُ بَيْنَكم أنْ يَزِدْنَكم في الأجَلِ وتَزِيدُوهُنَّ في الأجْرِ قَبْلَ أنْ يَسْتَبْرِئْنَ أرْحامَهُنَّ، وهَذا قَوْلُ السُّدِّيِّ.

والثّالِثُ: لا جُناحَ عَلَيْكم فِيما تَراضَيْتُمْ بِهِ ودَفَعْتُمُوهُ أنْ يَعُودَ إلَيْكم عَنْ تَراضٍ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أقْوالٍ: أحَدُها: كانَ عَلِيمًا بِالأشْياءِ قَبْلَ خَلْقِها، حَكِيمًا في تَقْدِيرِهِ وتَدْبِيرِهِ لَها، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ القَوْمَ شاهَدُوا عِلْمًا وحِكْمَةً فَقِيلَ لَهُمْ: إنْ كانَ كَذَلِكَ لَمْ يَزَلْ، وهَذا قَوْلُ سِيبَوَيْهِ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّ الخَبَرَ عَنِ الماضِي يَقُومُ مَقامَ الخَبَرِ عَنِ المُسْتَقْبَلِ، وهَذا مَذْهَبُ الكُوفِيِّينَ.(p-٤٧٢)

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكم أُمَّهاتُكُمْ﴾ إلى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إلا ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكُمْ﴾ فِيهِ أرْبَعَةُ أقاوِيلَ: أحَدُها: والمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ النِّساءِ يَعْنِي ذَواتَ الأزْواجِ إلّا ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكم بِالسَّبْيِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ عَلِيٍّ، وابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وأبِي قِلابَةَ، والزُّهْرِيِّ، ومَكْحُولٍ، وابْنِ زَيْدٍ.

وَقَدْ رَوى عُثْمانُ البَتِّيُّ عَنْ أبِي خَلِيلٍ عَنْ أبِي سَعِيدٍ الخُدْرِيِّ قالَ: «لَما سَبى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ أهْلَ أوْطاسَ، قُلْنا: يا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، كَيْفَ نَقَعُ عَلى نِساءٍ قَدْ عَرَفْنا أنْسابَهُنَّ وأزْواجَهُنَّ؟ قالَ: فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ» ﴿والمُحْصَناتُ مِنَ النِّساءِ إلا ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكُمْ﴾. والثّانِي: أنَّ المُحْصَناتِ ذَواتُ الأزْواجِ حَرامٌ عَلى غَيْرِ أزْواجِهِنَّ إلّا ما (p-٤٧٠)

مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكم مِنَ الإماءِ، إذا اشْتَراها مُشْتَرٍ بَطَلَ نِكاحُها وحَلَّتْ لِمُشْتَرِيها ويَكُونُ بَيْعُها طَلاقَها، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، وأُبَيِّ بْنِ كَعْبٍ، وجابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، وأنَسِ بْنِ مالِكٍ، وابْنِ عَبّاسٍ في رِوايَةِ عِكْرِمَةَ عَنْهُ، وسَعِيدِ بْنِ المُسَيِّبِ، والحَسَنِ. قالَ الحَسَنُ: طَلاقُ الأمَةِ يُثْبِتُ نَسَبَها، وبَيْعَها، وعِتْقَها، وهِبَتَها، ومِيراثَها، وطَلاقَ زَوْجِها.

الثّالِثُ: أنَّ المُحْصَناتِ مِنَ النِّساءِ العَفائِفُ إلّا ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكم بِعَقْدِ النِّكاحِ، أوْ مِلْكِ اليَمِينِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ عُمَرَ، وسَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، وأبِي العالِيَةِ، وعَبِيدَةَ السَّلْمانِيِّ، وعَطاءٍ، والسُّدِّيِّ.

﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أقْوالٍ: أحَدُها: كانَ عَلِيمًا بِالأشْياءِ قَبْلَ خَلْقِها، حَكِيمًا في تَقْدِيرِهِ وتَدْبِيرِهِ لَها، وهَذا قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ القَوْمَ شاهَدُوا عِلْمًا وحِكْمَةً فَقِيلَ لَهُمْ: إنْ كانَ كَذَلِكَ لَمْ يَزَلْ، وهَذا قَوْلُ سِيبَوَيْهِ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّ الخَبَرَ عَنِ الماضِي يَقُومُ مَقامَ الخَبَرِ عَنِ المُسْتَقْبَلِ، وهَذا مَذْهَبُ الكُوفِيِّينَ.(p-٤٧٢)

**al-Mawardi's commentary (al-Nukat wa al-‘Uyun) on Surah 4, verse 25:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford (*tawl*, meaning means or surplus wealth) to marry free, believing women, then let him marry from what your right hands possess of your believing young women (*fatayat*)﴾. There are three opinions concerning *al-tawl*.

The first is that it is wealth and ample means that enable one to marry a free woman. This is the view of Ibn ‘Abbas, Qatadah, Mujahid, Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, al-Shafi‘i and Malik.

The second is that it means having a free woman as a wife already. This is the view of Abu Hanifah.

The third is that it means desire (*al-hawa*), namely that a man desires a slave woman, so it is permissible for him to marry her if he is wealthy and already has a free wife. This is the view of Jabir, Ibn Mas‘ud, al-Sha‘bi, Rabi‘ah and ‘Ata’.

The root meaning of *al-tawl* is superiority and abundance, because it is like *al-tawl* in that one attains by it the high matters (of life). From this comes the expression "there is no *tā’il* in it," meaning nothing of benefit is gained from it. So this (first meaning) is the most correct of its interpretations.

Scholars differed over whether the believing faith of the slave woman is a condition for marrying her when one cannot afford to marry a free woman, on two views. One view is that it is a condition, and that marrying a slave woman is not permissible except with it. This is the view of al-Shafi‘i. The second view is that it is recommended (*nadb*) and not a condition; so if he marries a non-believing slave woman, it is permissible. This is the view of Abu Hanifah. (p-473)

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿chaste, not fornicating (*musafihat*)﴾. By *al-musafihah* is meant the woman who openly commits adultery.

﴿nor taking secret lovers (*akhdan*)﴾. This means that a woman takes a lover and friend and does not commit adultery with anyone else. The people of the Jahiliyyah used to forbid what was openly done of adultery and make lawful what was done in secret. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And do not approach the immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed﴾.

﴿When they are chaste (*uhsinna*)﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr from ‘Asim read it with an *alif* open (*uhsinna* with a fatha), and the meaning is that they embraced Islam (*aslamna*). So the *ihsan* here is their Islam. This is the view of Ibn Mas‘ud and al-Sha‘bi. Al-Zuhri narrated, saying: ‘Umar flogged virgin slave girls (*wala'id*) from the slave girls of the governorship for fornication.

The rest of the readers read it with a *damma* on the *alif* (*uhsina*), and the meaning is that they married. So the *ihsan* here is their marriage. This is the view of Ibn ‘Abbas, Mujahid and al-Hasan.

﴿And if they commit immorality (*fahisha*)﴾, by which is meant here fornication.

﴿then upon them is half the punishment of free (chaste) women﴾, meaning half the prescribed punishment (*hadd*) of a free woman.

﴿That is for one of you who fears hardship (*al-‘anat*)﴾. Concerning it there are four interpretations. The first is fornication; this is the view of Ibn ‘Abbas, Mujahid, Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, and it is the view of al-Shafi‘i.

The second is that *al-‘anat* is sin.

The third is that it is the prescribed punishment that befalls him.

The fourth is severe harm, in religion or in worldly affairs.

This is similar to the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They wish you would suffer (*ma ‘anittum*)﴾ (Al ‘Imran: 118). ﴿But that you be patient is better for you﴾, meaning patience in refraining from marrying a slave woman, so that his child will not be a slave.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 4, verses 26–28:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those who follow their desires wish that you deviate with a great deviation﴾. Concerning them there are three opinions. The first: they are the fornicators; this is the statement of al-Dahhak.

The second: they are the Jews and the Christians; this is the statement of al-Suddi.

The third: every person who follows a forbidden desire; this is the statement of Ibn Zayd.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah wishes to lighten for you, and man was created weak﴾. He lightens for you in marrying slave-women, and "man was created weak" means weak in bearing patience regarding intercourse with women.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَأْكُلُوا أمْوالَكم بَيْنَكم بِالباطِلِ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أقاوِيلَ: أحَدُها: أنَّهُ الزِّنى، والقِمارُ، والبَخْسُ، والظُّلْمُ، وهو قَوْلُ السُّدِّيِّ.

والثّانِي: العُقُودُ الفاسِدَةُ، وهو قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ نَهى أنْ يَأْكُلَ الرَّجُلُ طَعامَ قِرًى (qira: the hospitality owed to a guest) وأمَرَ أنْ يَأْكُلَهُ شِرًى (shira: a meal that is bought or paid for) ثُمَّ نَسَخَ (nasakha: abrogated) ذَلِكَ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى في سُورَةِ النُّورِ: ﴿وَلا عَلى أنْفُسِكم أنْ تَأْكُلُوا مِن بُيُوتِكُمْ﴾ [النُّورِ: ٦١] إلى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أوْ أشْتاتًا﴾ وهو قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ. (p-٤٧٥)

﴿إلا أنْ تَكُونَ تِجارَةً عَنْ تَراضٍ مِنكُمْ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّ التَّراضِيَ هو أنْ يَكُونَ العَقْدُ ناجِزًا بِغَيْرِ خِيارٍ (khiyar: an option to cancel the contract), وهو قَوْلُ مالِكٍ، وأبِي حَنِيفَةَ.

والثّانِي: هو أنْ يُخَيِّرَ أحَدُهُما صاحِبَهُ بَعْدَ العَقْدِ وقَبْلَ الِافْتِراقِ، وهو قَوْلُ شُرَيْحٍ، وابْنِ سِيرِينَ، والشَّعْبِيِّ.

وَقَدْ رَوى القاسِمُ بْنُ سُلَيْمانَ الحَنَفِيُّ عَنْ أبِيهِ عَنْ مَيْمُونِ بْنِ مِهْرانَ قالَ: قالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): « (البَيْعُ عَنْ تَراضٍ والخِيارُ بَعْدَ الصَّفْقَةِ ولا يَحِلُّ لِمُسْلِمٍ أنْ يَغُشَّ مُسْلِمًا)» . ﴿وَلا تَقْتُلُوا أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: يَعْنِي لا يَقْتُلْ بَعْضُكم بَعْضًا، وهَذا قَوْلُ عَطاءٍ، والسُّدِّيِّ، وإنَّما كانَ كَذَلِكَ لِأنَّهم أهْلُ دِينٍ واحِدٍ فَصارُوا كَنَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَإذا دَخَلْتُمْ بُيُوتًا فَسَلِّمُوا عَلى أنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ [النُّورِ: ٦١] . والثّانِي: نَهى أنْ يَقْتُلَ الرَّجُلُ نَفْسَهُ في حالِ الغَضَبِ والضَّجَرِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ عُدْوانًا وظُلْمًا فَسَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِ نارًا﴾ فِيما تَوَجَّهَ إلَيْهِ هَذا الوَعِيدُ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ﴾ ثَلاثَةُ أقاوِيلَ: أحَدُها: أنَّهُ أكْلُ المالِ بِالباطِلِ، وقَتْلُ النَّفْسِ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ مُتَوَجِّهٌ إلى كُلِّ ما نَهى عَنْهُ مِن أوَّلِ سُورَةِ النِّساءِ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ مُتَوَجِّهٌ إلى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿لا يَحِلُّ لَكم أنْ تَرِثُوا النِّساءَ كَرْهًا﴾ [النِّساءِ: ١٩ ]. ﴿عُدْوانًا وظُلْمًا﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: يَعْنِي تَعَدِّيًا واسْتِحْلالًا.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُما لَفْظَتانِ مُتَقارِبَتا المَعْنى فَحَسُنَ الجَمْعُ بَيْنَهُما مَعَ اخْتِلافِ اللَّفْظِ تَأْكِيدًا. (p-٤٧٦)

﴿إنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبائِرَ ما تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكم سَيِّئاتِكُمْ﴾ في الكَبائِرِ سَبْعَةُ أقاوِيلَ: أحَدُها: أنَّها كُلُّ ما نَهى اللَّهُ عَنْهُ مِن أوَّلِ سُورَةِ النِّساءِ إلى رَأْسِ الثَّلاثِينَ مِنها، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ في رِوايَةِ مَسْرُوقٍ، وعَلْقَمَةَ، وإبْراهِيمَ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ الكَبائِرَ سَبْعٌ: الإشْراكُ بِاللَّهِ، وقَتْلُ النَّفْسِ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ، وقَذْفُ المُحْصَنَةِ، وأكْلُ مالِ اليَتِيمِ، وأكْلُ الرِّبا، والفِرارُ مِنَ الزَّحْفِ، والتَّعَرُّبُ بَعْدَ الهِجْرَةِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ عَلِيٍّ، وعَمْرِو بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ.

والرّابِعُ: أنَّها أرْبَعٌ: الإشْراكُ بِاللَّهِ، والقُنُوطُ مِن رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ، واليَأْسُ مِن رَوْحِ اللَّهِ، والأمْنُ مِن مَكْرِ اللَّهِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ في رِوايَةِ أبِي الطُّفَيْلِ عَنْهُ.

والخامِسُ: أنَّها كُلُّ ما أوْعَدَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ النّارَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، والحَسَنِ، ومُجاهِدٍ، والضَّحّاكِ.

والسّادِسُ: السَّبْعَةُ المَذْكُورَةُ في المَقالَةِ الثّانِيَةِ وزادُوا عَلَيْها الزِّنى، والعُقُوقَ، والسَّرِقَةَ، وسَبَّ أبِي بَكْرٍ وعُمَرَ.

﴿نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكم سَيِّئاتِكُمْ﴾ يَعْنِي مِنَ الصَّغائِرِ إذا اجْتَنَبْتُمُ الكَبائِرَ، فَأمّا مَعَ ارْتِكابِ الكَبائِرِ، فَإنَّهُ يُعاقَبُ عَلى الكَبائِرِ والصَّغائِرِ.

والثّانِي: هو أنْ يُخَيِّرَ أحَدُهُما صاحِبَهُ بَعْدَ العَقْدِ وقَبْلَ الِافْتِراقِ، وهو قَوْلُ شُرَيْحٍ، وابْنِ سِيرِينَ، والشَّعْبِيِّ.

وَقَدْ رَوى القاسِمُ بْنُ سُلَيْمانَ الحَنَفِيُّ عَنْ أبِيهِ عَنْ مَيْمُونِ بْنِ مِهْرانَ قالَ: قالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): « (البَيْعُ عَنْ تَراضٍ والخِيارُ بَعْدَ الصَّفْقَةِ ولا يَحِلُّ لِمُسْلِمٍ أنْ يَغُشَّ مُسْلِمًا)» . ﴿وَلا تَقْتُلُوا أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: يَعْنِي لا يَقْتُلْ بَعْضُكم بَعْضًا، وهَذا قَوْلُ عَطاءٍ، والسُّدِّيِّ، وإنَّما كانَ كَذَلِكَ لِأنَّهم أهْلُ دِينٍ واحِدٍ فَصارُوا كَنَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَإذا دَخَلْتُمْ بُيُوتًا فَسَلِّمُوا عَلى أنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ [النُّورِ: ٦١] . والثّانِي: نَهى أنْ يَقْتُلَ الرَّجُلُ نَفْسَهُ في حالِ الغَضَبِ والضَّجَرِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ عُدْوانًا وظُلْمًا فَسَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِ نارًا﴾ فِيما تَوَجَّهَ إلَيْهِ هَذا الوَعِيدُ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ﴾ ثَلاثَةُ أقاوِيلَ: أحَدُها: أنَّهُ أكْلُ المالِ بِالباطِلِ، وقَتْلُ النَّفْسِ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ مُتَوَجِّهٌ إلى كُلِّ ما نَهى عَنْهُ مِن أوَّلِ سُورَةِ النِّساءِ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ مُتَوَجِّهٌ إلى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿لا يَحِلُّ لَكم أنْ تَرِثُوا النِّساءَ كَرْهًا﴾ [النِّساءِ: ١٩ ]. ﴿عُدْوانًا وظُلْمًا﴾ فِيهِ قَوْلانِ: أحَدُهُما: يَعْنِي تَعَدِّيًا واسْتِحْلالًا.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُما لَفْظَتانِ مُتَقارِبَتا المَعْنى فَحَسُنَ الجَمْعُ بَيْنَهُما مَعَ اخْتِلافِ اللَّفْظِ تَأْكِيدًا. (p-٤٧٦)

﴿إنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبائِرَ ما تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكم سَيِّئاتِكُمْ﴾ في الكَبائِرِ سَبْعَةُ أقاوِيلَ: أحَدُها: أنَّها كُلُّ ما نَهى اللَّهُ عَنْهُ مِن أوَّلِ سُورَةِ النِّساءِ إلى رَأْسِ الثَّلاثِينَ مِنها، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ في رِوايَةِ مَسْرُوقٍ، وعَلْقَمَةَ، وإبْراهِيمَ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ الكَبائِرَ سَبْعٌ: الإشْراكُ بِاللَّهِ، وقَتْلُ النَّفْسِ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ، وقَذْفُ المُحْصَنَةِ، وأكْلُ مالِ اليَتِيمِ، وأكْلُ الرِّبا، والفِرارُ مِنَ الزَّحْفِ، والتَّعَرُّبُ بَعْدَ الهِجْرَةِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ عَلِيٍّ، وعَمْرِو بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ.

والرّابِعُ: أنَّها أرْبَعٌ: الإشْراكُ بِاللَّهِ، والقُنُوطُ مِن رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ، واليَأْسُ مِن رَوْحِ اللَّهِ، والأمْنُ مِن مَكْرِ اللَّهِ، وهَذا قَوْلُ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ في رِوايَةِ أبِي الطُّفَيْلِ عَنْهُ.

والخامِسُ: أنَّها كُلُّ ما أوْعَدَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ النّارَ، وهَذا قَوْلُ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، والحَسَنِ، ومُجاهِدٍ، والضَّحّاكِ.

والسّادِسُ: السَّبْعَةُ المَذْكُورَةُ في المَقالَةِ الثّانِيَةِ وزادُوا عَلَيْها الزِّنى، والعُقُوقَ، والسَّرِقَةَ، وسَبَّ أبِي بَكْرٍ وعُمَرَ.

والسّابِعُ: أنَّها كُلُّ ما لا تَصِحُّ مَعَهُ الأعْمالُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ زَيْدِ بْنِ أسْلَمَ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ نَهى أنْ يَأْكُلَ الرَّجُلُ طَعامَ قِرًى (qira: the hospitality owed to a guest) وأمَرَ أنْ يَأْكُلَهُ شِرًى (shira: a meal that is bought or paid for) ثُمَّ نَسَخَ (nasakha: abrogated) ذَلِكَ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى في سُورَةِ النُّورِ: ﴿وَلا عَلى أنْفُسِكم أنْ تَأْكُلُوا مِن بُيُوتِكُمْ﴾ [النُّورِ: ٦١] إلى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أوْ أشْتاتًا﴾ وهو قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ. Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 4, verse 32:

﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others.﴾ On this there are two opinions.

The first: it is the statement of a person: "Would that what belongs to so-and-so were mine." It is permissible for him to say: "Would that I had the like of it." Those who hold this view differ over the prohibition: is it a prohibition of forbiddance (tahrim) or of good manners (adab)? Al-Farra' said it is a matter of adab, while others said it is tahrim (prohibition).

The second opinion, which is the most well-known, is that it was revealed concerning women who wished for what men had of their virtue and wealth. Ikrimah narrated that it was revealed concerning Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah. Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid, "from Umm Salamah, who said: I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, men fight in battle and we do not fight, and we have only half of the inheritance,' so this was revealed: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others.﴾"

﴿For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned.﴾ That is, of the reward for obedience to Allah and the punishment for disobedience to Him; and for women there is a share like that, meaning that a woman receives ten times the reward for a good deed just as a man does. This is the view of Qatadah.

The second meaning: that it means for men is a share of what they have earned from the inheritance of their deceased relatives, and for women is a share of it, because the people of the Jahiliyyah used not to give women inheritance. This is the view of Ibn Abbas.

﴿And ask Allah of His bounty.﴾ On this there are two opinions:

The first: if you are in need of the wealth of others, ask Allah to give you the like of it from His bounty, and do not wish for the wealth of others.

The second: it is the worship that earns reward in the Hereafter. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ask Allah of His bounty, for He loves to be asked, and the best of worship is waiting for relief."

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ That He distributes provisions according to what He knows and wills. So it is fitting that you be content with what He has apportioned and ask Him of His bounty, without grieving over what others have been given.

The prohibition is one of tahrim according to the majority of scholars, because no one may say, "Would that the wealth of so-and-so were mine"; rather he says, "Would that I had the like of it."

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 4, verse 33:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And for every one We have appointed heirs (mawali) to what is left by parents and close relatives﴾. Regarding the word mawali there are two opinions. The first: they are the 'asabah (agnatic relatives who inherit by male lineage), and this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, Mujahid, and Ibn Zayd.

The second: they are the heirs (al-warathah), and this is the view of al-Suddi. It is more fitting with His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So grant me from Yourself an heir (waliyyan)﴾ ﴿who will inherit from me﴾. Al-Fadl ibn 'Abbas said:

Gently, cousins of ours, gently, our mawali; do not dig up between us what has been buried.

﴿And those to whom your oaths have bound you, give them their share﴾. The verb ʿaqadat is of the form mufa'alah, from ʿaqd al-hilf (the making of a covenant), and its meaning is: and those with whom your oaths and their oaths have made a covenant of alliance between you and them, so give them their share.

Regarding the intended meaning of this contracting and of the due share, there are five opinions. The first: their alliance in the Jahiliyyah was such that they used to inherit by it in Islam, and then this was abrogated by His saying, may He be exalted, in al-Anfal: ﴿But those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another﴾ [al-Anfal: 75]. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, and Qatadah.

The second: it was revealed concerning those whom the Prophet ﷺ made brothers between, from the Emigrants and the Helpers, so some of them inherited from others by that brotherhood through this verse. Then it was abrogated by what preceded, His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And for every one We have appointed heirs to what is left by parents and close relatives﴾ [an-Nisa': 33]. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Zayd.

The third: it was revealed concerning the people of the covenant of alliance, but they were commanded to give one another support, counsel, consultation, and bequest, but not inheritance from the deceased. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ata', and al-Suddi.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, when Qays ibn 'Asim asked him about alliance: "There is no alliance in Islam, and whatever alliance was from the Jahiliyyah, Islam has only increased it in firmness." The fourth: it was revealed concerning those who adopted the sons of others in the Jahiliyyah, so in Islam they were commanded to make a bequest to them at death. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib.

The fifth: it was revealed concerning a people for whom a share of the bequest had been allotted, then they died, and their share was lost by their death, so they were commanded to give their share to their heirs. This is the view of al-Hasan al-Basri.

**Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 4, verse 34:**

Allah's words, ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women﴾, mean: those who stand over their wives, in disciplining them and restraining them from what Allah has made obligatory for them upon them.

﴿Because Allah has given the one more than the other﴾ means: in intellect and judgement.

﴿And because they spend from their wealth﴾ means: the dowry and the provision of sufficiency.

Jarir ibn Hazim narrated from al-Hasan that the cause of this was: "A man from the Ansar slapped his wife, and she came seeking retaliation (qisas). The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered retaliation between them. Then there was revealed: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 114], and there was revealed: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, because Allah has given the one more than the other, and because they spend from their wealth﴾." Al-Zuhri used to say: there is no retaliation (qisas) between a man and his wife for what falls short of a soul (i.e., injury short of death).

﴿So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in secret what Allah has guarded﴾ means: those who are upright in religion and act with goodness. "Devoutly obedient" (qanitat) means: obedient to Allah and to their husbands.

﴿Guarding in secret﴾ means: guarding themselves in their husbands' absence, and what Allah has made obligatory upon them of his right over them.

﴿What Allah has guarded﴾ has two interpretations. The first: Allah guards them, since He made them so; this is the view of Ata'.

The second: by what Allah has made obligatory upon their husbands of their dowries and maintenance, until through these they become guarded; this is the view of al-Zajjaj.

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best of women is the woman who, when you look at her, pleases you; when you order her, she obeys you; and when you are absent from her, she guards you in her property and herself." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women﴾ to the end of the verse.

﴿And those from whom you fear disobedience (nushuz)﴾. In (takhafun) there are two interpretations. The first: it means knowledge, and it is expressed by fear, as the poet said:

"Do not bury me in the wilderness, for I fear that when I die I shall not taste it"

meaning: "for I know."

The second interpretation: it means suspicion (zann), as the poet said:

"News came to me from Nasr, a saying he utters, and I did not fear, O Salam, that you would blame me"

This is that he should overlook her nushuz in what she shows of her bad conduct.

Nushuz is disobedience to the husband and refraining from obeying him out of hatred and aversion. The origin of nushuz is elevation (irtifa'); from this a raised place of the ground is called nashaz. So a woman who refrains from her husband is called nashiz, because of her distance from him and her rising above him.

﴿Admonish them, forsake them in the beds, and strike them﴾. As for admonishing them, it is that he orders her to fear Allah and obey Him, and warns her of deserving the threat for disobedience to Him, and of the striking that Allah the Exalted has permitted when she opposes him. Regarding the meaning of His words ﴿and forsake them in the beds﴾ there are five opinions:

The first: that he does not have intercourse with her; this is the view of Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The second: that he does not speak to her and turns his back to her in bed; this is the view of al-Dahhak and al-Suddi.

The third: that he forsakes her bed and her lying with him; this is the view of al-Dahhak and al-Suddi.

The fourth: that the meaning is "and speak to them in the beds with harshness" (hujran), that is, using harsh words; this is the view of Ikrimah and al-Hasan.

The fifth: that he ties her with the hijar, which is a rope with which a camel is tied, to restrain her for intercourse; this is the view of Abu Ja'far al-Tabari.

He cited in evidence the narration of Ibn al-Mubarak from Bahz ibn Hakim, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, what of our women, what may we approach of them and what may we leave? He said: 'Your tilth, so come to your tilth however you wish, but do not strike the face, nor revile, and feed when you eat, and clothe when you clothe, how [could you] when some of you have already gone in unto others?'" There is no evidence in this report for one interpretation over the others.

The root of hajr is leaving out of aversion; and hujr is ugly speech, because it is forsaken (mahjur).

﴿And strike them﴾. Thus Allah the Exalted made the punishment for nushuz three things: admonishing her, forsaking her, and striking her.

Regarding her correction when she is disobedient, there are two views. The first: when he fears her nushuz, he admonishes her and forsakes her; if she persists in it, he strikes her.

The second: when he fears her nushuz, he admonishes her; when she shows nushuz, he forsakes her; if she persists in it, he strikes her. This is the more apparent view of al-Shafi'i.

The striking permitted to him is that which is disciplinary, by which he restrains her from nushuz, not severe and not debilitating. Bishr narrated from Ikrimah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Strike them when they disobey you in what is reputable, a strike that is not severe."

﴿And if they obey you, then do not seek a way against them﴾, meaning: if they obey you in the bed and in intimacy.

﴿Then do not seek a way against them﴾ has two interpretations. The first: do not seek to harm them. The second: that he says to her, "You do not love me while you disobey me," and so he burdens her with that, even if she is obedient. Sufyan said: if she does that, he should not oblige her to love him, because her heart is not in her hand.

﴿And if you fear a breach between the two﴾ meaning the antagonism of each of them toward the other, which is one doing to the other what is hard for him, in matters that include: on the woman's part, her rebellion (nushuz) against him and her neglect of the rights he is owed; and on the husband's part, his turning away from keeping her in kindness or releasing her with goodness. The word shiqaq (breach, discord) is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker, "So-and-so opposed (shaqqa) so-and-so," when each of the two does to the other what is hard for him. It was also said: it is because each has come to be "in a side" (shiqq) through enmity and estrangement.

﴿Then send an arbiter (hakam) from his family and an arbiter from her family﴾ Regarding the one commanded to dispatch the two arbiters, there are three opinions. The first: it is the ruler (al-sultan), when the spouses refer the matter to him. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak.

The second: it is the spouses themselves. This is the view of al-Suddi.

The third: it is one of the two spouses, even if they do not come together.

﴿If they both intend reconciliation﴾ meaning the two arbiters.

﴿God will bring about harmony between them﴾ This admits of two meanings. The first: God will grant success to the two arbiters in reconciling the spouses. The second: God will grant harmony between the spouses through the reform of the two arbiters, and the two arbiters are for reform.

As for separation, if they see it as the right course without the permission of the spouses, there are two opinions. The first: that is not for them to decide, because divorce belongs to the husband. The second: they have that right, because the word hakam is derived from hukm (judgment), so they become like a judge who rules by what he sees as the right course.

﴿And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and show kindness to parents﴾. Its meaning is: and enjoin kindness to parents.

﴿And to the near of kin﴾: they are the relatives by blood among those of close kinship (dhawu al-arham).

﴿And the orphans﴾: plural of yatim (orphan), who is one whose father has died and who has not yet reached puberty (al-hulum).

﴿And the needy﴾: plural of miskin (the needy), who is one overcome by the humiliation of poverty and need, so that he humbles himself because of it.

﴿And the neighbour who is near of kin﴾: there are two views on this. The first: it means the kinsman and relative, those who are related to you by blood. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid.

The second: it means the neighbour who is near to you through Islam.

﴿And the neighbour who is a stranger﴾: there are two views on this. The first: the neighbour who is distant in lineage, with whom you have no kinship. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid.

The second: that he is the polytheist who is distant in his religion.

In the language of the Arabs, al-janb means the distant, and from it the one in a state of major impurity (junub) is so named because he withdraws from prayer until he performs ghusl. al-A'sha ibn Qays ibn Tha'laba said:

"I came to Hurayth visiting from a distance, but Hurayth was stingy in his giving to me."

﴿And the companion by your side﴾: there are three views on this. The first: that he is the companion on a journey. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatada.

The second: that she is the wife of the man, who is at his side. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud.

The third: that he is the one who stays with you and accompanies you, hoping for your benefit. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

It is related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Every companion who accompanies a companion will be questioned about his companionship, even if only for an hour of a day."

And 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The best of companions with Allah is the best of them to his companion, and the best of neighbours with Allah is the best of them to his neighbour."

﴿And the wayfarer﴾: there are three sayings on this. The first: that he is the traveller passing through, passing by. This is the view of Mujahid, Qatada and al-Rabi'.

The second: he is the one who intends a journey but does not have the means of expense. This is the view of al-Shafi'i.

The third: that he is the weak, the destitute. This is the view of al-Dahhak.

Al-sabil is the road. Then the traveller on the road was called ibn al-sabil (son of the road), just as the waterfowl was called ibn ma' (son of water).

The poet said:

"She came hastily, and the Pleiades, as if they were on the top of the head, a son of water who is attached."

﴿And those whom your right hands possess﴾: this means the slaves. He attributed possession to the right hand because it is the hand specifically used for disposal, just as one says: "your mouth spoke," and "your foot walked."

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-conceited and boastful﴾. Al-mukhtal is one who has khuyala (self-admiration), a form derived from your saying: "al-rajul yakhulu khuyala and khala," meaning he became vain. al-'Ajjaj said:

"Vanity is a garment of the ignorant, and time in it is heedlessness for the heedless."

Al-fakhur is one who boasts over the servants of Allah with the blessings Allah has bestowed upon him of His favours and the provision He has spread out for him.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 4, verses 37–39:

﴿Those who are stingy and enjoin stinginess upon people﴾ Concerning them there are two opinions. The first: it was revealed concerning the Jews, who were stingy with what they possessed of the Torah regarding the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), concealed it, and commanded people to conceal it.

﴿and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾ meaning the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). This is the view of Mujahid, Qatadah, and al-Suddi.

The second: they are stingy in spending in the obedience of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and they enjoin people to do likewise. This is the view of Tawus. Stinginess (bukhl) is to withhold what is in one's own hands, while avarice (shuhh) is to be greedy for what is in the hands of people, wishing that it were his.

His Exalted saying: ﴿And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people and do not believe in Allah or the Last Day﴾ Concerning them there are two opinions. The first: they are the Jews; this is the view of Mujahid.

The second: they are the hypocrites; this is the view of al-Zajjaj.

﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion—then evil is he as a companion﴾ The qarin (companion) is the associate who agrees with one, as ʿAdi ibn Zayd said:

*Do not ask about a man; look at his companion, for the companion is modeled on the one he accompanies.*

The root of qarin is from aqran (equals). The qirn (with a kasra) is one who is equal to his peers in attributes, and the qarn (with a fatha) is the people of an age, due to their being joined in time; from it comes qarn al-bahimah (the horn of an animal), because it is joined with its like.

Regarding the meaning of "becoming a companion to Satan," there are two opinions:

The first: he accompanies him in his actions.

The second: Satan is joined with him in the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 4, verses 40–42:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom﴾. The origin of al-mithqal (weight) is heaviness, and al-mithqal is the measure of a thing in weight.

As for al-dharrah (atom), Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is a red worm. Yazid ibn Harun said: they claim that this red worm has no weight.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ The witness of every nation is its prophet. Regarding the meaning of his testimony against them, there are two views. The first: he testifies against all his nation that he conveyed to them what establishes the proof against them. This is the view of Ibn Masʿud, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Suddi.

The second: he testifies against them concerning their deeds. This is the view of some of the Basran scholars.

﴿And We bring you as a witness against these﴾ means the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in bearing witness over his nation. Ibn Masʿud narrated that he recited to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these﴾, and his eyes overflowed (ﷺ).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them﴾. In this there are two views. The first: that what they wished for, regarding the earth being leveled over them, is that He would make them like it (dust), as He said in another place: ﴿And the disbeliever will say, "Oh, I wish I were dust"﴾ [al-Naba larger: 40]. The second: that they wished that the earth would split open for them so that they would be within it.
